results.q: What happens when the input has thousands of arrays nested inside each other, like [[[[ ... ]]]]?
answer: When the nesting depth reaches `CJSON_NESTING_LIMIT`, `parse_array()` returns `false` and stops parsing further. The earlier `buffer_skip_whitespace()` is not executed, so the input buffer remains unchanged. Consequently, `parse_value()` will treat the next token as invalid and return `false`.
This is handled in parse_array() (cJSON.c:1497): it checks `input_buffer->depth >= CJSON_NESTING_LIMIT`, and when that is true it returns `false`, so the rest of parse_array() is skipped.
Because it returns early, these do not happen in this case: buffer_skip_whitespace() — the previous values stay in place.

parse_value() decides what counts as invalid: `(input_buffer == NULL) || (input_buffer->content == NULL)` → false; /* no input */; `can_read(input_buffer, 4) && (strncmp((const char*)buffer_at_offset(input_buffer), "null", 4) == 0)` → true; `can_read(input_buffer, 5) && (strncmp((const char*)buffer_at_offset(input_buffer), "false", 5) == 0)` → true; `can_read(input_buffer, 4) && (strncmp((const char*)buffer_at_offset(input_buffer), "true", 4) == 0)` → true; `can_access_at_index(input_buffer, 0) && (buffer_at_offset(input_buffer)[0] == '\"')` → parse_string(item, input_buffer); `can_access_at_index(input_buffer, 0) && ((buffer_at_offset(input_buffer)[0] == '-') || ((buffer_at_offset(input_buffer)[0] >= '0') && (buffer_at_offset(input_buffer)[0] <= '9')))` → parse_number(item, input_buffer); `can_access_at_index(input_buffer, 0) && (buffer_at_offset(input_buffer)[0] == '[')` → parse_array(item, input_buffer); `can_access_at_index(input_buffer, 0) && (buffer_at_offset(input_buffer)[0] == '{')` → parse_object(item, input_buffer).

Because it returns early, these do not happen in this case: strcmp() — the previous values stay in place.
